text: In 2008 two oil spills from a pipeline operated by Shell's Nigerian subsidiary, the Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria (SPDC), polluted the Bodo area of the Niger Delta. SPDC admitted liability for the spills in proceedings in the English High Court, and in a settlement announced in January 2015 agreed to pay £55 million: £35 million for 15,600 individuals and £20 million for the Bodo community.

source.name: High Court of England and Wales (Technology and Construction Court), Akenhead J: The Bodo Community & Ors v The Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria Ltd [2014] EWHC 1973 (TCC) (The National Archives, Find Case Law)
source.quote: said to have occurred between 28 August and 7 November 2008 and 7 December 2008 and 19 February 2009; the full extent of the spillages and their timing is in dispute. Subject to such disputes Shell admit liability under the OPA for these spillages.

additionalSources.name: Amnesty International: Nigeria: Long-awaited victory as Shell finally pays out £55 million over Niger Delta oil spills
additionalSources.quote: Shell has always accepted that the two 2008 Bodo oil spills were the fault of failures on the company’s pipeline at Bodo

additionalSources.name: Leigh Day (solicitors for the Bodo community): Shell - Bodo (case page)
additionalSources.quote: The pipeline was operated by the Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria ltd, a subsidiary company of the oil giant, Shell.
